doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Ross with Kai Winding, Goodman and Doc Cheatham
summary: Ross worked in his late teens with Kai Winding's trombone group and played in Goodman's big band and sextet with Doc Cheatham.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Yeah, I was with his group early, I was in my late teens. I think I was 19 years old and I was working with Kai Winding. And some other friends of ours, Johnny Mesa and Carl Fontana.
Oh, yeah, that was a nice group. Four trombones and rhythm. Great.

And I’d been briefly with Benny Goodman’s big band when I was even younger than that I think, maybe 18-1/2. And then later I played with his small group, the sextet. The trumpet player was Doc Cheatham, who is now ninety-some years old and still playing.
Yeah, we were fortunate enough to talk with him.
Did you? Oh you talked to Doc?
I know he’s got plenty of stories.
I’m not positive about his age. I think he’s maybe 92? Something like that?
Uh, yeah. 91 or 92. And he talked about that particular band and how he had to kind of go back to school a little bit because he had been playing lead, and doing a lot of Latin —
Yeah I knew he did a lot of Latin work.
You know in a small group, having to solo quite a bit, an adjustment.
